mstts:express-as.prosody: As we wrap up, let’s take a moment to really let this sink in. Reclaiming your heart isn’t something you do just once—it’s a gentle practice, an everyday turning away from what doesn’t last, and moving toward what truly matters. Sure, you’ll face days filled with pain, disappointment, or uncertainty. But you’ll also find surprising strength, little sparks of joy, and a deep kind of peace that sticks with you, no matter what’s going on around you. So, here’s what to remember as you move forward: Gratitude has this quiet power—it softens pain and helps you spot abundance, even in the middle of loss. Forgiveness? It’s like setting your heart free from old wounds and anger. When you live with real intention, even your smallest choices start to feel meaningful. And when you open up to change, your heart gets the space it needs to grow and explore new possibilities. Most of all, anchoring your heart in what truly lasts brings you a peace that doesn’t fade. Here’s something to hold onto: you don’t have to have it all figured out before you start. Healing isn’t about getting it perfect—it’s about being present, showing up for your own life, one moment at a time. Some days, old patterns and aches might sneak back in. That’s just part of being human. But every time you choose gratitude over bitterness, forgiveness instead of resentment, or intention over old habits, you reclaim just a little more of your heart. So, be gentle with yourself. Trust that every single step—even the hard ones—are moving you closer to the freedom and peace you’re after. The world’s always going to throw distractions your way, but you get to decide where your heart calls home. With patience, a little faith, and the courage to let go, you can always find your way back—again and again. Because your heart was made to return.
